title: Agreement of split procedures
statement: For natural numbers $C,e$ and a Boolean word $w$, the following two results agree: search the integers from $0$ through $|w|$ for the first index $i$ satisfying $i+C(i+1)^e=|w|$, and, if found, encode the prefix of $w$ of length equal to the loop counter after $i$ iterations of the rule that appends a true bit whenever the counter's length is at most $|w|$; otherwise return the empty word. This equals the encoding of the prefix of length $i$ and the corresponding suffix when the equation has a solution in that range, and is empty when it does not.
